verdict: THEORY HOLDS AT SCALE, SPEED STILL NEUTRAL, DIGIT-DENSE LEVER REJECTED AT THE FIRE-RATE BAR. (1) Compile scaled and got FASTER: 13874 probe rows (3.2x C1), 8 horizons (2x C1), closed-form compile 8.07s, bit-exact recompile, heads 321KB RAM-resident; probe crossed 2 slices (445s+48s) with disclosed resume, every slice <= 460s. (2) Verify/reason generation stays accuracy-exact: B strict 0.3667 == A strict 0.3667 (0.0pp difference), 28/30 token-identical (divergences are fp near-tie argmax flips, not mechanism errors). (3) Speed ratio B/A = 1.0104 (MARGINAL band [0.95,1.10)): fire rate rose 5.29% -> 7.01% but stays under the 8% partial bar -> H1 lever REJECTED per frozen band; acceptance 0.901 and avg 2.15 tokens/fire-iteration mean verify overhead still cancels block savings. (4) The digit-dense format COSTS the base model: A strict 36.7% vs C1 verbose 50.0% (-13.3pp, outside the frozen +/-10pp stability band -> H4 FAIL); C blind-fire drops to 0.2667 (-10.0pp) re-confirming the reason-over-blocks step is necessary. HONEST BOTTOM LINE: more data into the same closed-form compile scales cleanly and cheaply (this is the data->weight side of the big run working), but the tok/s win needs a different lever than format: the fire/tau policy (lower tau with acceptance-aware budget) or batched verify, not more probe rows.
